name: vision_multitask
title: A shared-backbone detection + segmentation trainer on the 2024 PyTorch stack: channels_last, torch.compile, bfloat16 autocast and gradient accumulation
origin: domain-vision round 2: three idioms that read like defects and are not - bf16 autocast with no GradScaler, zero_grad/step inside an accumulation guard, and a model rebound to torch.compile() before the optimizer is built

forbidden.why: there is no sklearn transformer in this project
the training loader is built with shuffle=True
the validation loader is built with shuffle=False
the loaders are built inside build_loaders(), reached only from main() under the __main__ guard
eval_augment() is LongestMaxSize, PadIfNeeded, Normalize and ToTensorV2 - no random stage at all. The six random stages live in train_augment()
THE TRAP: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) runs once before the loop and again inside `if (step + 1) % accum == 0`, which is what gradient accumulation is
THE TRAP: optimizer.step() sits inside the same accumulation guard, which the rule's If-descent is documented to handle
loss.backward() precedes the guarded step, and the zero_grad inside the guard runs after it - which is the correct accumulation order, not the backward -> zero_grad -> step inversion
the only no_grad region is the decorated evaluate(), which contains no backward()
the running total accumulates losses["total"].item()
OneCycleLR is a per-batch schedule and scheduler.step() runs inside the batch loop, on the accumulation boundary, with steps_per_epoch computed to match
THE TRAP: there is no GradScaler and there should not be one. bfloat16 carries fp32's exponent range, so there is nothing to scale; adding a scaler is the mistake here
clip_grad_norm_ runs between the backward and the step, inside the accumulation guard
evaluate() calls model.eval() before the loop and model.train() on the way out
evaluate() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator
the mask is thresholded and the class is argmax-ed before either is compared
the detection class branch returns raw logits and MultiTaskLoss pairs it with nn.CrossEntropyLoss - the correct pairing; there is no softmax in this project

THE TRAP: SegmentationHead returns logits, mask_bce is nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss, and the sigmoid at line 114 is inside soft_dice, which is a different term that needs probabilities. The producer of the BCE input never reaches a sigmoid
the sigmoid in evaluate() is applied to the head's logits for thresholding, not for a loss
the model and the criterion are moved with .to(device) and move() moves the images and every target tensor inside both loops
pick_device() checks torch.cuda.is_available()
seed_everything() seeds random, numpy, torch and torch.cuda
the split is two directories on disk; nothing is split at run time
ConvNormAct, Encoder, SegmentationHead, DetectionHead, MultiTaskNet and MultiTaskLoss all chain super().__init__()
the encoder stages are wrapped in nn.ModuleList
the checkpoint saves model.state_dict()

unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV211 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `forbidden`, original note: THE TRAP: the model is rebound to torch.compile(model) BEFORE torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters()) is built, so the optimizer already owns the compiled module's parameters
